lede: It opens with the angels drawn up in rows and closes with their own words: “We are those ranged in ranks; we are those who glorify.” Between the two it tells of a father and a son who both submitted, and of a prophet in the belly of a fish.

names.name: al-Ṣāffāt
names.note: After the oath it opens with. They are the angels, in the saying of Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, ʿIkrimah, Mujāhid, Qatādah and the majority: standing in rows in the heavens before their Lord.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all: Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī both record the agreement. The traditional order places it fifty-sixth.

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ الصّافّاتِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
أحَدُهُما: أنَّها المَلائِكَةُ، قالَهُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ، وابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، وسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وقَتادَةُ، والجُمْهُورُ

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهْ والبَيْهَقِيُّ في ”الدَّلائِلِ“ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ سُورَةُ ”الصّافّاتِ“ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: The Arabs of Makkah had filled the unseen world with relations of Allah. The angels, they said, were His daughters. The jinn were His kin. The soothsayers’ jinn listened at the gates of heaven and brought down its secrets. This surah takes that picture apart piece by piece.

It begins with the angels as they are: ranged in ranks, driving, reciting — servants in formation, swearing that “your God is One.” The lowest heaven is adorned with stars and guarded against every rebellious devil; whoever tries to snatch a word is pursued by a piercing flame. Near the end the angels speak for themselves: “There is none of us but has a known station. We are those ranged in ranks, and we are those who glorify.” The Prophet ﷺ pointed his Companions to that picture when he taught them how to stand in prayer.

The centre of the surah is a gallery of messengers, each told in a few ayat and each closing on the same blessing — “Peace upon Nūḥ among the worlds… Peace upon Ibrāhīm… Peace upon Mūsā and Hārūn… Peace upon Ilyās.” The longest is Ibrāhīm’s: the idols broken, the fire, the migration, and then the dream. “My son, I see in my sleep that I am sacrificing you; so look, what do you think?” — “Father, do what you are commanded. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the patient.” When both had submitted, and he had laid him on his forehead, the call came: you have fulfilled the vision. And a great sacrifice was given in ransom.

The Qurʾan does not name the son here. Ibn Kathīr argues that the passage itself shows he was Ismāʿīl — the good news of Isḥāq comes only afterwards, as a further gift — and says that the other view, that it was Isḥāq, is found in neither Book nor Sunnah and was most likely taken from the scholars of the People of the Book.
Yūnus comes last: the laden ship, the lot, the fish. “Had he not been one of those who glorify, he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are raised.”

occasions.title: Which son
occasions.text: Ibn Kathīr notes that a group of the scholars held the son to be Isḥāq, and that this is even reported from some of the Companions. “That is in neither Book nor Sunnah,” he writes, “and I think it was only taken from the rabbis of the People of the Book, and accepted without proof. Here is the Book of Allah, a witness and a guide to its being Ismāʿīl”: it tells of the forbearing son and the sacrifice, and only then says, “and We gave him good news of Isḥāq.”

evidence.quote: وَقَدْ ذَهَبَ جَمَاعَةٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ إِلَى أَنَّ الذَّبِيحَ هُوَ إِسْحَاقُ، وَحُكِيَ ذَلِكَ عَنْ طَائِفَةٍ مِنَ السَّلَفِ، حَتَّى نُقِلَ عَنْ بَعْضِ الصَّحَابَةِ أَيْضًا، وَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ فِي كِتَابٍ وَلَا سُنَّةٍ، وَمَا أَظُنُّ ذَلِكَ تُلقى إِلَّا عَنْ أَحْبَارِ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ، وَأُخِذَ ذَلِكَ مُسَلَّمًا مِنْ غَيْرِ حُجَّةٍ. وَهَذَا كِتَابُ اللَّهِ شَاهِدٌ وَمُرْشِدٌ إِلَى أَنَّهُ إِسْمَاعِيلُ

aim: To declare Allah far above what the idolaters ascribed to Him, and to demolish their claims about the angels and the jinn.
themes: The people of the Garden and the Fire

outline.title: The oath
outline.summary: By those ranged in ranks, those who drive with force, those who recite the Reminder: your God is One — Lord of the heavens and the earth, and Lord of the risings. We have adorned the nearest heaven with the stars, and guarded it against every rebellious devil; they cannot listen to the highest assembly, and are pelted from every side.

outline.title: The Day of Decision
outline.summary: Ask them: are they harder to create, or those others We created? When reminded, they do not remember; they say, “When we are dust and bones, shall we be raised?” It will be a single cry. “Gather the wrongdoers and their kind, and what they used to worship… and stop them: they are to be questioned.” They turn on one another, followers and leaders. They were the ones who, when told “There is no god but Allah,” grew proud and said: “Shall we give up our gods for a mad poet?”

outline.title: The chosen servants, and the tree of Zaqqūm
outline.summary: But the chosen servants of Allah have a known provision: fruits, and honour, in gardens of delight, on thrones, with a cup from a flowing spring. One of them says: “I had a companion who used to say, ‘Are you really one of those who believe that when we are dust we shall be judged?’” He looks, and sees him in the midst of Hell: “By Allah, you nearly ruined me.” For the like of this let the workers work. Is that the better welcome, or the tree of Zaqqūm, which grows in the root of Hell, its fruit like the heads of devils?

outline.title: Nūḥ, and Ibrāhīm
outline.summary: Nūḥ called upon Us — and how excellent are those who answer. And of his kind was Ibrāhīm, who came to his Lord with a sound heart. He broke the idols; they built a fire for him; he said, “I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.” We gave him good news of a forbearing son. When the boy was old enough to work beside him: “My son, I see in a dream that I am sacrificing you.” — “Father, do as you are commanded.” When they had both submitted, We called to him: “You have fulfilled the vision.” We ransomed him with a great sacrifice — and gave him good news of Isḥāq, a prophet among the righteous.

outline.title: Mūsā and Hārūn, Ilyās, Lūṭ, Yūnus
outline.summary: We favoured Mūsā and Hārūn and saved them and their people. Ilyās said to his people, “Do you call on Baʿl and leave the best of creators?” We saved Lūṭ and his family. And Yūnus: he fled to the laden ship, drew lots and lost, and the fish swallowed him. Had he not been of those who glorify, he would have stayed in its belly till the Day of Resurrection. We cast him on the bare shore, sick, and grew a gourd-plant over him, and sent him to a hundred thousand or more; they believed.

outline.title: Daughters? Kin?
outline.summary: So ask them: does your Lord have daughters while they have sons? Did We create the angels female while they watched? They have made a kinship between Him and the jinn. Glory be to Allah above what they describe. “There is none of us but has a known station. We are those ranged in ranks, and we are those who glorify.”

outline.title: The word already given
outline.summary: Our word has already gone forth to Our servants the messengers: it is they who will be helped, and it is Our host that will prevail. So turn from them for a while. Glory to your Lord, the Lord of might, above what they describe; and peace upon the messengers; and praise to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

keyAyah.why: A father’s question and a son’s answer. The Arabic word for what they both did next is the root of the word Islam.

virtues.text: “Will you not form your rows as the angels form their rows before their Lord?” We said: “Messenger of Allah, how do the angels form their rows before their Lord?” He said: “They complete the first rows, and stand close together in the row.”
virtues.arabic: أَلاَ تَصُفُّونَ كَمَا تَصُفُّ الْمَلاَئِكَةُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهَا

virtues.text: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to tell us to keep the prayer light, and he would lead us with al-Ṣāffāt.”

before: Yā-Sīn ended with the dominion of all things in His hand. Al-Ṣāffāt opens with the highest of His creatures standing in ranks before Him.
after: Al-Ṣāffāt ends: Our host will prevail — so turn from them for a while. Ṣād opens on the leaders of Quraysh walking out, and tells him: be patient with what they say, and remember Our servant Dāwūd.
